assumptions: all binary patterns of length 2..10 (2044 patterns)
codeword counts by exact dynamic programming (big integers), growth rates from the denominator x^k + (1-2x) c_p(x)
falsification: A length-k pattern other than 0^k, 1^k with lambda >= lambda_(1^k); a range of large n where a pattern beats 1^k of the same length (refutes H-C11-2).
hypothesis: H-C11-1: among binary patterns of length k, exactly 1^k and 0^k maximise the growth rate lambda_p (hence the asymptotic efficiency 1/log2 lambda_p). H-C11-2 (bold, inventor): for every n beyond a small threshold, the best length-k terminator is 1^k. H-C11-3: unbordered patterns of length k have lambda equal to the (k-1)-bonacci constant.
methodology: Compute lambda_p two ways (polynomial root; count ratio at length 400); rank patterns; compare cumulative codeword counts of 1^k with unbordered patterns; compute, for every n <= 2^64, the pattern of length <= 8 giving the shortest codeword (envelope) and crossover points against Elias gamma/delta/omega/Levenshtein; OEIS checks of count sequences.
question: How does the terminator pattern p control the code T_p? Is 1^k best among patterns of length k?
